disposition: REPAIR_REQUIRED: expert mathematical source review and typed countermodel/repair contracts. Lean proofs have not been accepted.
source: Orabona, arXiv:1912.13213v10, Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 on printed 34, Theorem 4.3 first item on printed 35–36 (PDF 46–48).
original: For proper convex f, λ-strong convexity on dom ∂f is printed as equivalent to strong monotonicity of all its subgradients there. The inventory and printed theorem remain unchanged.

example.objective: For t>0, f=s²+t²; for t=0, f=max(s²,1); for t<0, f=+∞.
example.supported: All points of positive height have support 2(s,t). At height zero there is a subgradient exactly at |s|≥1, and all of them are (2s,b) with b≤0.
example.consequence: All support pairs satisfy the printed inequality with λ=2. At (-1,0) and (1,0) both values are 1, the squared distance is 4, and the midpoint value 1 exceeds the required upper bound 0. The midpoint belongs to dom f but not dom ∂f.

repair: Use an explicit convex carrier V contained in dom ∂f. Both the quadratic penalty and the strong monotonicity constant refer to the chosen original norm. The coordinate pairing may be transported by a linear equivalence; no isometry is assumed.
consumer: The weighted entropy result uses the repair on the positive weighted simplex and the true ℓ¹ norm. The already proved pairing does not establish strong convexity on its own.
remaining: Formalize properness and actual real epigraph convexity, full support classification, λ=2 globally on supported points and failure at the midpoint.
Complete the convex-carrier equivalence and all public canaries, project, reader and semantic checks before accepting row 149.
